title: Which Weighs More: a Kilogram of Steel or Feathers?
description:
The obvious answer is also the correct one—but the details get interesting.

They have equal mass and, in the same location, essentially equal weight: one kilogram each.

The feathers occupy more volume and experience a slightly larger buoyant force from air; exact high-precision scale readings depend on how mass is calibrated.

In a vacuum the buoyancy difference disappears.
